helperTranscript.text: Answer directly from the following supplied evidence; no additional file inspection or tool calls are needed. Scope is a diagnosis/recovery recommendation, not execution. Parent verified via PowerShell.MCP: HTTP input at log line47389 is {title:'[Proposed v2] Discover and select a delegation target',priority:0,createBasicFlow:false}, NO Scope; corresponding SQL log47359 still reports old overlong Scope. Entity UseCaseEntity.Scope StringLength50. CreateUseCaseCommandHandler adds entity then SaveChanges; catch returns Failure(ex.Message,ex) without detach/clear. QBrainAi.Cqrs/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs24 registers Dispatcher singleton. Dispatcher.cs25 stores injected IServiceProvider; line93 resolves handler via _services.GetRequiredService(handlerType). Handler constructors take McpDbContext. Thus failed EF tracked inserts can remain under root-provider lifetime. Service restarted14:39, plugin ListAsync now shows exactly7 baseline UCs and no12 proposed titles. Corrected pending payloads use Scope 'Proposed v2 / unapproved / proposed-v2' (36 chars), FR-FRENEMY-101..112, Realizes links, createBasicFlow=false, unapproved/proposed provenance in briefDescription. Recommend duplicate-safe save/readback sequencing and distinguish confirmed truncation from inferred retained-context mechanism. Also note separate RDP default helper resolution limitation; this session uses supported explicit agentPath and CODEX_HOME. Start FINAL ANSWER: and give the substantive answer now from supplied evidence.

The supplied evidence confirms the Scope length failure. `UseCaseEntity.Scope` permits 50 characters, and SQL still received the original overlong value even though HTTP input at line 47389 contained only `title`, `priority`, and `createBasicFlow:false`. Removing Scope from that later request did not remove the value reaching SQL.

Retained EF tracking is the likely mechanism, but it is not conclusively proven. The create handler adds the entity before `SaveChanges` and leaves it tracked after failure. The singleton Dispatcher resolves handlers through its stored provider; handlers receive `McpDbContext`. That combination can retain a failed insert when resolution uses a context held by the root provider. Context identity and tracking evidence would establish the precise lifetime involved.

The restart at 14:39 provides a clean recovery checkpoint: plugin `ListAsync` now returns exactly seven baseline use cases and none of the twelve proposed titles. This confirms their absence from that readback; it does not independently prove the tracking mechanism.

Recommended duplicate-safe recovery through the required plugin:

1. Before each create, use `ListAsync` to check for the exact proposed title and provenance. If a match exists, read it back and reconcile its fields and links before considering another create.
2. Save one proposed use case at a time with Scope `Proposed v2 / unapproved / proposed-v2`, `createBasicFlow:false`, and the unapproved/proposed provenance in `briefDescription`. That Scope is **38 characters**, within the 50-character limit.
3. Read back the returned ID and verify title, Scope, provenance, unapproved status, and absence of an automatically generated basic flow. Create or verify its intended Realizes link to the corresponding requirement in `FR-FRENEMY-101` through `FR-FRENEMY-112`, then read back that link before proceeding.
4. On any failure or ambiguous response, stop further creates and check persisted state before retrying. Another smaller payload cannot repair an already tracked failed entity.

The code correction should give each dispatch a properly scoped handler/context lifetime and discard the failed unit of work after a save failure. Returning `Failure(ex.Message, ex)` alone does not reset EF tracking.

The RDP helper limitation is separate: default executable/profile resolution lacks a console user in that environment. This diagnostic session’s supported explicit `agentPath` and `CODEX_HOME` address helper startup. They do not explain the UC persistence failure or waive plugin guardrails.
